Using RiboPilot with your group of organisms

Source: vignettes/Reference-Databases.Rmd
Reference-Databases.Rmd

To assemble a sample, RiboPilot compares its reads to known ribosomal sequences from related organisms. It comes ready to use for ray-finned fishes. For any other group, you build that reference data once, and it is reused for every future project on that group.

You do not need to find or format any sequences yourself. RiboPilot downloads them from GenBank for you.

Build reference data for a group

Use build_reference_db(). It takes a standard NCBI search (the same kind of query you would type on the NCBI website) and a short label for the group. It then downloads the relevant 18S, 5.8S, 28S, and ITS sequences and prepares the reference data.

# 1. First, just check how many sequences are available. Nothing is downloaded.
RiboPilot::build_reference_db(
  '"Gastropoda"[Organism]', "gastropoda",
  count_only = TRUE, conda_env = "ribopilot"
)

# 2. Then build the reference data and save it somewhere you can reuse.
db <- RiboPilot::build_reference_db(
  '"Gastropoda"[Organism]', "gastropoda",
  out_dir = "~/ribopilot_refs", conda_env = "ribopilot"
)

Replace Gastropoda with your group. The "[Organism]" part tells NCBI to search by organism name, so '"Gastropoda"[Organism]' means “all gastropod sequences”. The second value, "gastropoda", is just a short label used in the file names.

Running this needs the tools you installed with conda, so start R from a terminal where you have run conda activate ribopilot, or keep the conda_env = “ribopilot” setting shown above.

Use it in a project

When you set up a project, point it at the reference data you built by adding two lines to new_project():

RiboPilot::new_project(
  path       = "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn = "~/my_samples.csv",
  data_path  = "~/my_reads",
  executor   = "conda",
  custom_seeds_db  = db$seeds,
  custom_labels_db = db$labels
)

Good to know

  • Build once, reuse forever. If you run build_reference_db() again for the same group and location, it reuses what you already built instead of re-downloading. To force a fresh rebuild, add overwrite = TRUE.
  • Where it is saved. If you leave out out_dir, RiboPilot saves the reference data in a default folder on your computer and finds it automatically next time. Setting out_dir to a shared location lets your whole lab reuse the same data.
  • Groups with few sequences. Some groups have very little published ribosomal data. If your search returns only a handful of records (check with count_only = TRUE first), broaden it to a larger group. For example, search a whole family or order rather than a single genus, so RiboPilot has enough reference sequence to work with.
  • The 5.8S gene. GenBank rarely stores 5.8S on its own; it is usually bundled inside ITS records. That is fine: RiboPilot still recovers the 5.8S region from the full repeat, and its quality checks anchor on the 18S and 28S genes.
